We consider a collectively monitored spin model with a boundary time-crystalline phase, introducing inhomogeneity by partitioning the ensemble into two subsystems rotated by an angle $\theta$. We find that the measurement-induced phase transition survives under inhomogeneities, with different entanglement scaling regimes. The waiting time increases with $\theta$, scaling as $1/N$ but with a prefactor strongly enhanced by orders of magnitude, and in the anti-aligned limit $\theta = \pi$ it remains finite, fully resolving the resolution barrier. This mitigation, however, comes at a cost: the entanglement saturation time becomes significantly longer, partially reintroducing the postselection barrier. Our results highlight a trade-off between detector resolution and postselection overhead, with direct implications for the experimental observation of measurement-induced phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Tanbir Islam, Fernando Iemini

item.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
item.description: arXiv:2607.09051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum $XY$ model and the interacting disordered $XXZ$ chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.
item.dc:creator: Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Yun-Jie Wang, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Chao Wang, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo

item.title: Transferred QAOA Parameters Remember the Penalty Scale: A $\lambda$-Resonance Law for Constrained Quantum Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.09927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Training the variational angles of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm once on a small instance and reusing them on larger ones, known as parameter transfer, is the standard route past the exact-simulation wall. Existing literature explains its success almost entirely through structural similarity. We identify a new, independent axis that governs transfer whenever constraints are encoded as penalties: the trained angles memorize the penalty weight $\lambda$ of their training instance. For any scalarized cost function with an integer-valued violation count, we prove that at arbitrary fixed QAOA angles $(\beta,\gamma)$ of depth $p$, the probability mass $F(\lambda)$ on the feasible subspace is a finite real trigonometric polynomial in $\lambda$ whose angular frequencies lie on an integer lattice generated by the trained $\gamma$'s. Three consequences follow immediately: transfer feasibility is a resonance peaked where the deployment penalty matches the training penalty; the resonance width scales as $1/(v_{max}\sum_k|\gamma_k|)$, so low-$|\gamma|$ angle sets are systematically more transferable; and the curve exhibits revival peaks at spacings $2\pi/\gamma_k$. We confirm all three predictions by exact statevector experiments on a 20-qubit multi-user resource-allocation QUBO. The theorem is independent of how the angles were obtained and applies to any integer-penalty QUBO, recasting a widely reported failure mode of penalty-based QAOA as deterministic, predictable phase interference rather than an energetic tuning problem.
item.dc:creator: Krit Grover

item.title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
item.description: arXiv:2607.21551v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an unconditional construction of information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption for one-bit messages, with efficient encryption and decryption and exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage. Previous work by Bhattacharyya and Culf (Nature Physics, 2026) and Bhattacharyya, Broadbent, and Culf (arXiv:2603.08916) either only showed inverse-polynomial security loss or required inefficient encryption/decryption operations; we avoid both of these caveats. Our scheme's key is a uniformly random non-identity phase-free Pauli on $n$ qubits, and bit $a$ is encrypted as a random $(-1)^a$ eigenstate of that Pauli. We prove that the probability that both receivers recover the bit is at most $1/2 + O\left(2^{-n/2}\right).$ By a lower bound due to Broadbent, Culf, and Rochette (IACR Communications in Cryptology, 2026), this is the best probability bound achievable with $n$-qubit ciphertexts while ensuring perfect correctness (up to the constant hidden in the $O(\cdot)$).
item.dc:creator: Prabhanjan Ananth, Seyoon Ragavan, Amit Sahai

item.title: A Kernel-Based Density of States Estimator for Quantum Computing
item.description: arXiv:2607.24972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a quantum kernel method for estimating the density of states (DoS) of quantum many-body systems. The method exploits the Rodeo algorithm as a physical implementation, requiring no modification of its standard single-ancilla circuit. Averaging the Rodeo response over Haar-random input states reconstructs the DoS convolved with a spectral kernel whose analytical form is determined entirely by the probability distribution of the sampled evolution times. This establishes a direct quantum analogue of the classical Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM): Haar-random states perform stochastic trace estimation, while the temporal sampling distribution plays the role of the reconstruction kernel. We derive the estimator, quantify its statistical and systematic uncertainties, and establish an explicit correspondence between quantum reconstruction kernels and classical signal-processing window functions, enabling concepts such as spectral leakage, side-lobe attenuation, and main-lobe width to guide kernel design. The method is validated numerically on the one-dimensional transverse-field spin--$\sfrac{1}{2}$ and spin--$1$ Ising models, where the reconstructed density of states and the resulting thermodynamic observables agree with exact diagonalization within the estimated statistical uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha

item.title: Best Annealing Path of Simulated Quantum Annealing via Efficient Adiabatic Phase Transition
item.description: arXiv:2608.30282v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nested Simulated Annealing (NSA) is proposed for accelerating the classical simulation of Quantum Annealing (QA). NSA is based on two-spin interaction and exploits the causality of spin-flip, thereby significantly reducing computational cost. And through Unitary Coupled-Cluster (UCC) method, I establish a connection between NSA and XX interaction which is one of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians and demonstrate that NSA effectively utilizes a trivial degenerate state. Furthermore, by treating spins as continuous variables, I derive an energy formulation that incorporates both the problem Hamiltonian and the perturbation Hamiltonian induced by transverse electromagnetic field and show that the annealing path characterized by the lowest local-maximum exhibits the fastest convergence. Based on the result, I present a strategy for finding optimal annealing parameters for Simulated Quantum Annealing (SQA).
item.dc:creator: Kiyotaka Murashima

item.title: Multimode squeezed light generation and characterization
item.description: arXiv:2609.08591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nowadays, the realization of quantum computations and communications based on continuous variables has attracted significant attention due to a substantial expansion of the system dimensionality. The main progress in this area is attributed to the implementation of multimode systems based on squeezed states of light. One of the simplest ways to generate such states relies upon their producing in a single-pass optical parametric amplifier (OPA) under ultrafast pumping. However, for homodyne detection of such multimode states, the profile of the local oscillator (LO) must perfectly match the profile of the measured mode. Usually, this is not the case; therefore, a proper treatment of multimode squeezing is required. In this work, we study both theoretically and experimentally the multimode squeezed light generated in type-0 and type-II OPA. We characterize such sources using the Schmidt-mode representation and investigate the degree of squeezing depending on the LO spectral profile, employing a pulse shaping technique. In addition, we investigate cluster states that can be generated under the given experimental conditions. This work might have a significant impact on the realization of multimode quantum protocols.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Chudakov, Vladislav Severin, Anastasia Poshevkina, Danil Malyshev, Kirill Kuznetsov, Olga Tikhonova, Dmitry Kalashnikov, Polina R. Sharapova

item.title: qdmag: A Python package for simulating nonequilibrium magnetization of molecules using quantum master equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.16352v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present qdmag, a computational utility for calculating the magnetization of magnetic molecules in a time-varying external magnetic field by solving a generalized Lindblad quantum master equation with spin-phonon coupling treated as a dissipation term. The package relies on the spin Hamiltonian formalism, which includes both the magnetic exchange interactions and the zero-field splitting (ZFS) interaction. Different types of magnetic exchange interaction and ZFS terms up to 12th order, which are written in terms of the extended Stevens operators, are supported. qdmag enables long-time evolution of magnetization for up to a few milliseconds, which is achieved through a staircase approximation of the magnetic field as a function of time. For high-dimensional spin Hamiltonians, a lower-dimensional effective Hamiltonian is constructed to make the calculations computationally feasible. Three case studies of one-spin, two-spin, and three-spin systems are presented to demonstrate the usage of qdmag. Our work offers a computational tool to bridge the gap between theoretical development and numerical calculations of spin dynamics in the presence of spin-phonon coupling.
item.dc:creator: Shuanglong Liu, Xiao Chen, Andrew Cupo, James N. Fry, Hai-Ping Cheng

item.title: Entangled measurements are necessary for optimal tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states and of bosonic Gaussian states near the vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2609.23189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that learning an unknown mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes to trace distance $\epsilon$ requires $\Omega(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies when measurements act on one copy at a time, even with arbitrary POVMs, fresh ancillas and classical adaptivity, but without quantum memory between copies. The bound holds for $0<\epsilon\le1/3600$ and separates this model from the known collective rate $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. It follows from a uniform single-copy Fisher-information budget and a dimension-independent comparison between trace distance and Gaussian parameters. On covariance matrices of operator norm at most $1-c$, we prove a Frobenius-to-trace-norm continuity bound with constant $[2c(2-c)]^{-1/2}$; matchgate shadows then attain $O(m^3/(c\epsilon^2))$ copies. This also gives explicit error certificates for thermal free-fermion states. For a class of mixed passive bosonic Gaussian states with total mean photon number at most one, a reduction to bounded-block qudit tomography gives a single-copy lower bound $\Omega(m^3/(\epsilon^2\sqrt{\log(m/\epsilon)}))$, versus collective complexity $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. These separations answer the mixed-state measurement-resource question posed by Chen et al. A two-mode example has optimal two-copy Fisher trace $5$, versus the separable ceiling $4$. An IBM replication gave a pre-registered witness lower bound $4.12$ at one-sided $95\%$ shot-noise confidence; its interpretation assumes the prescribed preparations and a common measurement channel and does not bound preparation systematics.
item.dc:creator: Ron Rubin (Rubin Anders Scientific, Inc.)

item.title: Quantum error mitigation from information dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2609.31934v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Overcoming experimental errors is a central challenge in quantum science. This challenge is particularly acute in large and complex quantum circuits, where quantum information spreads into exponentially many paths, foiling any direct attempt to understand errors' impact. In this work, we present a novel approach to understanding and mitigating experimental errors, based on a surprisingly compact representation of a quantum circuit's information dynamics, the reactivity function. The shape of a circuit's reactivity function governs its noise response, and its amenability to different error mitigation methods. From this viewpoint, we introduce two complementary such methods. The first, Pauli-path zero-noise extrapolation, fits a parameterized model to a circuit's reactivity function and uses it to accurately extrapolate to zero noise. The second, tunable error cancellation, filters a circuit's reactivity function to cancel noise on all information up to a threshold locality. Crucially, both methods feature a tuning parameter that allows one to systematically improve their accuracy until convergence. Across three circuit families from published experiments, our methods overcome conventional zero-noise extrapolation biases as large as 30%; at $\sim$$10^{-2}$ root-mean-square error, they reduce sampling cost relative to probabilistic error cancellation by up to a factor of $10^3$.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Suchsland, Thomas Schuster, Manuel S. Rudolph, Nicholas Noll, Thomas E. O'Brien, Zlatko K. Minev

item.title: Cycle Codes and Decoded Quantum Interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.40036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) reduces optimization problems with two-variable constraints to decoding cycle codes. For one such problem, namely MaxCut, prior work showed that DQI achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee only on linear-girth graphs, for which MaxCut is classically easy. However, these no-go results rely on minimum distance assumptions that do not represent true decodability thresholds for common noise channels, thus underestimating actual DQI performance. To estimate the true performance, we derive DQI satisfaction guarantees in the presence of imperfect decoding for fixed instances and generalize prior results for random instances. We then study homological cycle codes over arbitrary finite fields and show that minimum-weight decoding is NP-hard for every field of size $q>2$, in contrast with known results for binary cycle codes. On the Linial--Simkin ensemble of regular graphs with logarithmic girth, we prove maximum-likelihood recovery bounds and a strong converse for a family of non-uniform additive noise channels. Moreover, linear programming (LP) decoders provide polynomial-time recovery of a positive fraction of randomly located errors with arbitrary values. These results allow us to prove upper and lower bounds on the approximate optima achievable by DQI when restricted to classical decoders. These bounds rule out quantum advantage in the regimes we analyze but also identify a family of regular Max-$k$-Cut instances on which DQI efficiently achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee.
item.dc:creator: Anuj Apte, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Andi Gu, Stephen P. Jordan, Ojas Parekh, Ruslan Shaydulin, Jacob Watkins, Noureldin Yosri, Adam Zalcman

item.title: Quantum Algorithms for OPI Variants Beyond Locality and Classical Decodability
item.description: arXiv:2610.00502v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Regev's reduction quantumly finds codewords satisfying nonlinear constraints by decoding the dual code. To date, applications that have not been dequantized have relied on efficient classical decoders and coordinate-wise constraints. We overcome these restrictions separately. Our first contribution uses a quantum decoder to find solutions $\mathbf{y}\in(\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\{0\})^m$ to $\mathbf{B}\mathbf{y}=0$, where $\mathbf{B}\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n\times m}$. For fixed prime $q>2$, Chen, Liu, and Zhandry solve this problem for random matrices with $m=\Omega(n^2)$, a regime now covered by classical algorithms. We adapt their template to codes (spanned by the rows of $\mathbf{B}$) that satisfy a "two-fold multiplication property": the coordinate-wise products of pairs of codewords span a space of dimension smaller than $m$. Under suitable distance conditions, this allows us to solve instances with $m\leq n^{2-\Omega(1)}$, beyond the established guarantees of classical algorithms. We also give an efficient classical algorithm under a stronger three-fold multiplication property, leaving intermediate regimes as candidates for quantum advantage. For Reed-Muller codes punctured at random points, our algorithm finds a word in the unpunctured dual code supported exactly on those points. This works beyond known efficient classical decoding regimes. Our second contribution retains classical decoding but allows global constraints on symbol frequencies. We study "histogram-local" constraints, which specify the allowed numbers of occurrences of each symbol. For broad families, stability under resampling one coordinate yields efficient quantum algorithms for variants of optimal polynomial intersection (OPI) combining coordinate-wise and histogram-local constraints. Adapting Yamakawa-Zhandry, we prove a quantum-classical separation for these problems relative to a classical random oracle.
item.dc:creator: Seyoon Ragavan, Noah Shutty

item.title: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a coupled three-dimensional double well, at an excited eigenstate
item.description: arXiv:2610.03362v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the coupled three-dimensional double well $H=\tfrac12|p|^2+2\sum_i(q_i^2-1)^2-\sum_{i<j}q_i^2q_j^2$ we exhibit, at the first excited energy level (and also at the ground state), a linear functional on polynomials of degree $\le 6$ that satisfies every constraint of the standard level-3 eigenstate bootstrap, has a strictly positive definite moment matrix, and nevertheless assigns a negative value to a nonnegative polynomial. It is therefore an interior point of the level-3 relaxation that is realized by no quantum state. The construction reflects a fact that holds at every level: the eigenstate rows never reach the top-degree momentum moments. At level 3, where strictly feasible points exist, this means that the corresponding block of the moment matrix carries no information about which energies admit one. Every algebraic ingredient is an exact rational certificate, and the only numerical ingredients (spectral enclosures of an eigenfunction) are carried out in rigorous ball arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Keren, Ye Zhou

item.title: Spurious zero-dispersion continua in full $(2,q)$-positivity: A linear hierarchy-depth lower bound from an exactly solvable counting operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.09698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Variational two-particle reduced-density-matrix methods impose hierarchies of semidefinite constraints. We ask whether a fixed level of such a hierarchy can recover even an elementary many-fermion spectrum, using the dispersion test, in which a value is accepted as an eigenvalue when the minimized dispersion vanishes. We study an exactly solvable operator that counts fermions in one half of the spin orbitals. It is a sum of commuting occupation numbers, so its spectral problem is classical, a Boolean occupation-number problem with integer spectrum, and the obstruction found here is not a genuinely quantum one. We determine the complete set of accepted values at every level of the full hierarchy of particle-hole semidefinite constraints. Besides the integers, this set contains an entire interval of noninteger values unless the hierarchy level grows linearly with the particle number, and we give the exact threshold. The proof constructs explicit q-positive reduced density matrices, diagonal in the occupation basis, by continuing the occupation probabilities of a fixed-particle-number state to a noninteger particle number. The fermionic content is that classical semidefinite constraints on occupation correlations, with nonnegative occupation-pattern probabilities, imply positivity of every particle-hole block, so the noncommuting fermionic conditions remove no false value. A converse argument shows that no other false eigenvalues occur. The limitation is specific to the hierarchy: two-body inequalities that encode the integer spectrum would remove every false value but are not generated at a fixed level. By Erdahl's duality theorem, whose hypotheses we check at fixed particle number, the result applies equally to the full (2,q)-positivity conditions of the constructive solution of the N-representability problem.
item.dc:creator: Maho Nakata

item.title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code's effective distance below threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.26785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Correlated decoding improves matching and clustering surface-code decoders by reweighting one decoding subgraph conditioned on the other's correction. We show that standard reweighting can cause correlated decoders to fail on size-$(d-1)/2$ fault configurations that a distance-$d$ code should correct, reducing error suppression deep below threshold. Under circuit-level noise, a single first-pass edge can discount several correlated edges, even though their joint occurrence requires additional independent faults, so the decoder favors an over-discounted correction. Regularizing the reweighting rule restores the nominal distance scaling and a clear correlated-decoding advantage.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Hernando de la Fuente, Joonas Majaniemi, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Felix Frohnert

item.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In classical cryptography, one-way functions are necessary for most of cryptography. In the quantum world, however, Kretschmer at {TQC'21} and subsequent works have demonstrated that quantum versions of various primitives in minicrypt, such as signatures and private-key encryption, do not require quantum-computable one-way functions (\textsf{qOWF}s). However, the question of the necessity of \textsf{qOWF}s for primitives in Cryptomania like public-key encryption with classical public keys and ciphertexts (\textsf{qPKE}) has remained open. We provide a comprehensive picture of the relationship between \textsf{qPKE} and \textsf{qOWF}. First, our main result is a black-box separation between \textsf{qOWF}s and \textsf{qPKE}. In particular, we show that relative to a unitary, real, and self-inverse oracle, there exists a \textsf{qPKE} scheme (with classical keys and ciphertexts), but \textsf{qOWF}s do not exist. Further, our oracles admit a point-function obfuscation construction, thus ruling out black-box construction of \textsf{qOWF} from point function obfuscations. On the positive side, we construct \textsf{qPKE} from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation for quantum circuits with classical obfuscated descriptions and efficiently verifiable one-way puzzles, which is known to be a potentially weaker assumption than \textsf{qOWF}s, due to an existing black-box separation. Our construction is the quantum analog of the classical construction of \textsf{PKE} from one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation in the quantum computation with classical communication (QCCC) setting.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Barhoush, Amit Behera

item.title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
item.description: arXiv:2611.08293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries. We demonstrate that matrix product operators enable the explicit construction of intertwiners between the dual theories and their (non-invertible) symmetries. With closed boundary conditions, we can relate the full spectrum of these dual theories by considering all possible twisted boundary conditions. We illustrate how the Peter-Weyl transform appears when the duality acts on the boundary Hilbert space of a $G$-symmetric model. The presented framework generalizes previous work on dualities for unitary fusion category symmetric models. It exemplifies how dualities for both finite and continuous symmetries rely on the relation between a bond algebra and a representation of the symmetry in the lattice as double centralizers. We argue that dual non-invertible spontaneous symmetry breaking is the mechanism that underlies symmetric tensor network algorithms. We illustrate these results for $U(1)$- and $SU(2)$-symmetric quantum lattice models.
item.dc:creator: Dante Bosgoed, Frank Verstraete, Laurens Lootens

item.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on Cayley graphs over dihedral groups
item.description: arXiv:2605.02254v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a complete classification of Cayley graphs over dihedral groups that exhibit perfect state transfer between distinct vertex states in Grover walks. For $n\ge 3$, let $D_n:=\langle a,b : a^n=b^2=1,\ bab=a^{-1}\rangle$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$, and let $S\subseteq D_n\setminus\{1\}$ satisfying $S=S^{-1}$ and $\langle S\rangle =D_n$. We show that the Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(D_n,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $(D_n,S)$ is equivalent to one of the following pairs: $(D_n,\{b,ba\})$; $(D_n,\{a,a^{-1},ba,ba^{-1}\})$, where $4$ does not divide $n$; or $(D_{2m},\{b,ba^{m},ba,ba^{m+1}\})$, where $m$ is odd. Our proof combines the representation theory of $D_n$ with tools from algebraic number theory.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya, Xiwang Cao

item.title: Effective skyrmion number for mixed polarization states of light
item.description: arXiv:2605.24293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polarization skyrmions are usually characterized through a unit Stokes vector field, which defines a map from the transverse plane to the Poincar\'e (Bloch) sphere and allows one to assign a skyrmion number under appropriate boundary conditions. This description assumes complete polarization. In many optical situations, however, the local polarization state is partially polarized and is therefore described by a spectral polarization matrix rather than by a single Jones vector. We formulate a density-matrix-based effective extension of the skyrmion-number construction for statistically stationary, quasi-monochromatic paraxial fields in terms of the normalized spectral polarization matrix. Its eigenvectors define two orthogonal polarization eigenstates, corresponding to antipodal points on the sphere, while the eigenvalue imbalance is fixed by the local degree of polarization (DoP) $P(\mathbf r)$. Averaging the opposite skyrmion-density contributions of these two eigenpolarizations leads to an effective skyrmion number in which the usual pure-state density is weighted by $P(\mathbf r)$. The resulting quantity reduces to the conventional skyrmion number for fully polarized fields and assigns zero weight to locally unpolarized regions. In general, it is not an integer topological invariant; rather, it is an integrated effective measure, constructed from local Stokes parameters, which can be interpreted geometrically as a DoP-weighted signed solid-angle integral of the polarization eigentexture on the Poincar\'e sphere. We illustrate the construction with a regular analytic family of polarization eigentextures with winding order $m$ and fixed radial DoP profiles, showing how the effective number depends jointly on the winding order and on the spatial overlap between the DoP and the skyrmion density.
item.dc:creator: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

item.title: A Physically-Realisable Quantum Programming Language with Quantum-Controlled Quantum Channels
item.description: arXiv:2607.15873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In contrast to a classical bit, which can only take the value $0$ or $1$, its quantum counterpart---a qubit---can exist in a superposition of $0$ and $1$. This is a superposition of data values, and it is then tempting to superpose programs as well. Indeed, a particular superposition of programs, known as the quantum SWITCH, has attracted considerable attention. A natural way to superpose programs is conditional branching on quantum data, and several studies have pursued this idea. However, there is a well-known semantic difficulty with this approach, and the fundamental question of whether the languages proposed in prior work can be physically realised remains open. This paper proposes a physically realisable quantum programming language with quantum branching over quantum channels. We first analyse the semantic difficulty from an implementation perspective and show that the difficulty is caused by arbitrariness in the implementation. We then design a language that is free from this arbitrariness. As expected from its implementation-oriented design, our language is physically realisable. We argue for this from two directions: first, we give a method for compiling programs into quantum circuits; and second, we show that our programs stay within the physically admissible range, namely, that they neither yield probabilities greater than one nor violate causal inequalities. The absence of such violations is established through the inclusion of our language in QC-QC, a notion of realisability studied in physics.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Hirata, Takeshi Tsukada

item.title: Schr\"{o}dinger Generator for High-Dimensional Integration and Sampling on Quantum Many-Body States
item.description: arXiv:2608.00529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integration and sampling in high dimensions are among central challenges in modern science and technology, underlying applications ranging from quantum many-body physics to Bayesian inference and artificial intelligence. Although conventional Monte Carlo methods are formally scalable, their efficiency deteriorates rapidly in the presence of strong correlations or sharp features in high-dimensional configuration space. Here we introduce a new framework, termed the Schr"odinger Generator, for integration and sampling based on the explicit optimization of coordinate transformations. The method decomposes the total Jacobian into two complementary components, including an adaptive map that minimizes estimator variance by learning the marginal structure in each dimension, and a normalizing-flow-based transformation that captures non-factorizable correlations in the target distribution. A final resampling step guarantees unbiased sampling even when the learned transformation is imperfect. We demonstrate stable and scalable performance for nuclear quantum many-body states in dimensions exceeding 600. Short-range correlations among nucleons in finite nucleus are faithfully reproduced. The framework offers a physically transparent approach to high-dimensional stochastic integration and sampling, opening new possibilities for simulations of complex quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Lin-Jing Jiang, Fu Ma, Pei Li, Kai-Jia Sun, Guo-Liang Ma, Yu-Gang Ma

item.title: Hidden transverse-flow topology in partially coherent structured light
item.description: arXiv:2608.14923v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Partial coherence is commonly viewed as a mechanism that reduces contrast or smooths intensity structure. Here we show that it can also encode hidden transverse-flow topology. Starting from the cross-spectral density, we formulate a generalized transverse flux, an effective velocity field, and the associated flux trajectories for quasi-monochromatic partially coherent paraxial beams. This construction converts two-point correlation phases into local transport information and reduces to the usual coherent energy-flow picture in the single-mode limit. Because the generalized flux is obtained through a local differential operation on the cross-spectral density, the proposed trajectories are, in principle, reconstructible from sufficiently resolved phase-sensitive measurements of the complex second-order coherence function, subject to the regularization required by numerical differentiation. Two analytical beam families expose this hidden topology. In twisted Gaussian Schell-model beams, a Gaussian intensity hides a distributed rotational flow with nonzero vorticity. In Laguerre-Christoffel-Darboux beams, sources with identical intensity profiles can have different flux topology, producing either spiral or purely radial trajectories. Thus, intensity and coherence magnitude do not exhaust the physical information contained in the cross-spectral density: partial coherence can reorganize the hidden topology of transverse optical transport.
item.dc:creator: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

item.title: Exact quantum geometry from sublattice symmetry: Closed-form solution of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model
item.description: arXiv:2608.26099v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum geometry has emerged as a guiding principle across atomic and condensed-matter physics, shaping the topological responses of Bloch bands and the stability of the correlated phases they host. Sublattice symmetry, though common among bipartite lattice models, has not yet been exploited to obtain closed-form quantum geometry in multiband systems. For this purpose, we derive a general expression for the QGT of sublattice-symmetric systems in terms of contributions from the individual sublattice sectors, and show that this symmetry renders the Bloch Hamiltonian of a paradigmatic four-band model, the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model, anti-block-diagonal, analytically yielding the spectrum, eigenstates, and full quantum geometric tensor (QGT), including the Berry curvature and quantum metric, for all four bands. The model, describing charged particles on a two-dimensional square lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field, has recently been realized experimentally with ultracold atoms, photons, and superconducting circuits. Finally, we evaluate fractional-Chern-insulator stability criteria analytically and quantify the lowest band of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model to be a nearly ideal Chern band. Our approach opens a route for studying also the quantum geometry of other sublattice-symmetric multiband systems.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Tesfaye, Andr\'e Eckardt

item.title: Revealing the Quantum Signature of Gravity via Gravitational Waves
item.description: arXiv:2609.09931v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can propagating gravitational waves serve as operational probes of the quantum nature of gravity? We address this question by developing a unified theoretical framework that combines spacetime geometry, quantum information, and gravitational-wave physics. Starting from the geodesic deviation equation in linearized General Relativity, we derive the effective detector Hamiltonian directly from spacetime geometry and construct the complete quantum dynamics for detector subsystems interacting with both classical and quantized propagating gravitational-wave fields. This unified formulation enables a direct comparison between classical and quantum descriptions of gravitational radiation within the same physical framework. We demonstrate that classical gravitational-wave backgrounds can induce mixedness in the detector state but cannot generate genuine quantum correlations between the detector subsystems. In contrast, quantized gravitational waves coherently mediate gravity-induced entanglement, quantum coherence, quantum memory, and nonclassical correlations, providing clear operational signatures of the quantum nature of propagating gravitational radiation. We further discuss how mesoscopic quantum mechanical oscillators offer a promising route towards experimentally probing these effects. Our results establish a geometric and quantum-information-based framework for exploring quantum gravity through propagating gravitational waves.
item.dc:creator: Partha Nandi

item.title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.23781v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.
item.dc:creator: Amir Nesturov, Attila Tak\'acs, Lenart Zadnik

item.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.37122v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler-extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997). Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $\delta\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $$ m+O_\alpha(\log(D/\delta))\text{ random bits and } O_\alpha\!\left(\varepsilon^{-2-\alpha}\log^{1+\alpha}(D/\delta)\right)\text{ samples}, $$ for any constant $\alpha>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1+\alpha} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_\alpha(a+\log(1/\eta))$ and seed length at most $(1+\alpha)\log a+(2+\alpha)\log(1/\eta)+O_\alpha(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $\eta$. We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-\Omega(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/\eta))$ and output length $\Omega(n)$, improving previous constructions.
item.dc:creator: Kuan Cheng, Ruiyang Wu

item.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
item.description: arXiv:2610.38338v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.
item.dc:creator: M. N. Kiselev
